The Why Have Sex? Questionnaire Short Form (YSEX-SF), administered on 24 September
2026, describes the respondent's reasons for having sex across 14 motivational domains. The
profile is best understood as a whole rather than through any single subscale score. The
respondent's most frequently endorsed reasons for having sex were Duty/Pressure, Social
Status, and Expression. The respondent's highest-scoring subscales are described in more
Score 10/10, corresponding to a frequency descriptor of 'All of my sexual
experiences'. This subscale reflects sex engaged in out of obligation or in response to pressure.
The respondent reports that all or almost all of their sexual experiences have been motivated by
this reason. The two items contributing to this score were answered as follows:
- 13. I was pressured into doing it. (All of my sexual experiences)
- 27. I felt obligated to. (All of my sexual experiences)
Score 8/10, corresponding to a frequency descriptor of 'Many of my sexual
experiences'. This subscale reflects sex used to enhance reputation or social standing. The
respondent reports that many of their sexual experiences have been motivated by this reason.
The two items contributing to this score were answered as follows:
- 7. I wanted to enhance my reputation. (Many of my sexual experiences)
- 21. I thought it would boost my status. (Many of my sexual experiences)
Score 8/10, corresponding to a frequency descriptor of 'Many of my sexual
experiences'. This subscale reflects sex used to mark occasions or communicate messages
such as welcome, farewell, or celebration. The respondent reports that many of their sexual
experiences have been motivated by this reason. The two items contributing to this score were
- 11. I wanted to welcome someone home or say goodbye. (All of my sexual experiences)

The respondent endorsed pressure or obligation as a reason for having sex (a response above
'None of my sexual experiences' on one or both items):
- 13. I was pressured into doing it. (All of my sexual experiences)
- 27. I felt obligated to. (All of my sexual experiences)
Motivations of this kind range from a sense of relational duty through to unwanted or coerced
experiences. Their meaning is best understood in conversation with the respondent.
Each of the 14 subscales is scored by summing its two items (response options 1 'None of my
sexual experiences' to 5 'All of my sexual experiences'), giving subscale scores from 2 to 10.
Higher scores indicate that a greater proportion of the respondent's sexual experiences have
been motivated by that reason. No total score is computed and no norms, percentiles, or clinical
cut-offs exist; the clinical output is the 14-subscale profile.
Each subscale score is accompanied by a frequency descriptor derived from the response
options (score 2 = 'None of my sexual experiences'; 3-4 = 'A few'; 5-6 = 'Some'; 7-8 = 'Many';
9-10 = 'All of my sexual experiences'). These descriptors are frequency labels, not severity
ratings: the clinical relevance of a given frequency depends on the motivation being assessed
The profile is interpreted relatively: the most clinically informative feature is which motivations
are most and least frequent for the respondent, rather than the value of any single subscale in
isolation. If either Duty/Pressure item ('I was pressured into doing it', 'I felt obligated to') is
endorsed above 'None of my sexual experiences', the report displays a note for the clinician, as
motivations of this kind range from a sense of relational duty through to unwanted or coerced

each reason would lead them to have sex, and their profile is read as anticipated rather than
